corrections_required.evidence: In s332-detail4-left and full-332.png the ל has a T-shaped qamats under it, and the final kaf has a two-dot sheva inside. That is the same mark as inside the kaf of חוֹשֶׁךְ (line 4). Compare לְךָ in line 16 (s332-detail2-left): there the ל has a sheva and the kaf has a qamats inside. The two forms look clearly different.

limitations: The images are at a fixed resolution and I could not zoom further. At this size I usually can't tell a segol or tsere alone from one with a meteg stroke, especially in the small-type odd-numbered lines. Where I lean towards a meteg, it is listed as a dispute, not asserted.

I checked every word on the page for metegs, including נֶעְלָם, וּבְיוֹשֶׁר and בֶּאֱמֶת. If I saw no stroke, that is not proof there is no meteg. Words where I saw nothing that looked like a candidate are not listed; at this resolution, that doesn't certify that they have no meteg.
The 5 provisional changes are confirmed by image only. I did not recompute input_sha256 or output_sha256.
The running head is cut off at the top and marked non-printing; I did not check it further.
This is a source-reading review only. There is no source approval and nothing is approved for XML, export, batch or leaf. No files were edited.
notes: Letter-level check: I compared all 28 lines word for word with full-332.png and the 8 detail images. Every word matches the snapshot's letters, with one exception: line 28 לְךָ should be לָךְ (see corrections_required).
